description: One entry per rule ID a scripts/qa checker prints (Plan 00484 G6). `llm_qa.py --explain <ID>` prints an entry. `checks` names the scripts that print the ID; tests/unit/qa/test_qa_rules.py fails when this file and the scripts disagree, in either direction.
batch_defences_description: The checkers listed as batch-check rows of `hooks-daemon defences`: each is the whole-tree form of a write-time handler's defect class. `step` is the llm_qa.py step that runs it, `defect_class` a DefectClass value. A spelling convention is not a defect class, so check_british_english.py is not listed. The rows are every rule below whose `checks` names the script.

american-spelling.statement: A British-English project wrote an American spelling.
american-spelling.fix: Use the British spelling. If the word is a quotation or an identifier, wrap it in backticks: inline code is not checked.

authored-path-stat.statement: A path built by joining an author-written value is stat-ed or read as joined, so a `..` in it is walked through the filesystem and the answer depends on every directory along the way existing.
authored-path-stat.fix: Normalise the path lexically first, with `utils.authored_paths.authored_path_exists`; for a read, normalise and then establish containment before opening. There is no exemption marker.

bare-except.statement: A bare `except:` catches everything, including KeyboardInterrupt, and hides the error.
bare-except.fix: Catch the specific exception types the call can raise, and handle or re-raise them.

bare-python-module.fix: Point the agent at the skill instead: `Skill tool: skill=hooks-daemon, args=<subcommand>`.

bootstrap-reexec-dollar0-source.statement: `$0`-relative path resolution (`dirname "$0"`, `${0%/*}`) appears after a self-bootstrap re-exec stanza, which relocates `$0` to a mktemp path, so a sibling lookup built on it breaks.
bootstrap-reexec-dollar0-source.fix: Anchor to a value derived from PROJECT_ROOT or DAEMON_DIR, or add `# shell-audit: allow -- <reason>` inline or on the line above if the reference genuinely predates the re-exec.

capability-table-drift.statement: `constants/events.py` says an event can or cannot block, and the vendored Claude Code contract says otherwise.
capability-table-drift.fix: Correct `can_block` for the event in `constants/events.py`, or refresh the vendored contract if it is stale.

capture-corruption.statement: A function whose stdout is captured (`var=$(func)`) or redirected to a file elsewhere writes to stdout somewhere other than its return position, so the caller's variable or file holds extra text.
capture-corruption.fix: Redirect diagnostics with `>&2`, write the value only at the function's terminal return, or add `# capture-audit: allow -- <reason>`.

cli-subcommand-unknown.statement: A shell-tagged fence runs `bin/hooks-daemon <subcommand>` with a subcommand the CLI does not have.
cli-subcommand-unknown.fix: Use a subcommand the CLI has, or use the skill (Skill tool: skill=hooks-daemon, args=<subcommand>); the wrapper exits 2 on an unknown one.

config.statement: The sensitive-content checker's own configuration is invalid, so the scan could not be trusted.
config.fix: Correct the `sensitive_content` options in `.claude/hooks-daemon.yaml` named in the finding.

config-key-mismatch.statement: In `docs/guides/HANDLER_REFERENCE.md` a handler section's `**Config key**` row names a different key from the section's own heading.
config-key-mismatch.fix: Make the heading and the `**Config key**` row name the same key: readers copy the row, not the heading.

config-unparseable.statement: The history sweep could not parse the configuration it reads, so the sweep did not complete.
config-unparseable.fix: Fix the YAML syntax of the config file the finding names.

conftest-subtree.statement: Test-selection rule: a test was selected because it lives under a conftest.py that the change touched.
conftest-subtree.fix: Not a defect. It explains why a test ran; see `scripts/qa/run_changed_tests.py` for the mapping.

daemon-dir-cd-in-docs.statement: A document tells the reader to `cd` into `.claude/hooks-daemon/`, which the daemon's CLI commands must not be run from.
daemon-dir-cd-in-docs.fix: Show the command run from the project root, for example `bin/hooks-daemon status`.

dangerous-invocation-corpus.statement: A recorded corpus verdict no longer describes what the daemon does: a dangerous outcome is reachable by a spelling no guard names.
dangerous-invocation-corpus.fix: Restore the handler behaviour, or correct the row in `scripts/qa/dangerous-invocation-corpus.yaml` with the reason the verdict changed.

dead-letter-field.statement: A schema accepts a field that the vendored docs say Claude Code discards for that event.
dead-letter-field.fix: Remove the field from that event's schema, or refresh the contract if Claude Code now honours it.

declared.statement: Test-selection rule: a test was selected because `changed_tests_map.yaml` declares it for a changed file.
declared.fix: Not a defect. It explains why a test ran; see `scripts/qa/changed_tests_map.yaml`.

declared-invariant-pairs.statement: Two sites a human declared as a pair no longer satisfy the declared relation (asymmetric sibling protection).
declared-invariant-pairs.fix: Change both sides together, or update the pair's row in `scripts/qa/declared-invariant-pairs.yaml`.

deleted-test.statement: Test-selection rule: a deleted test file is recorded so its removal is not mistaken for an unmapped change.
deleted-test.fix: Not a defect. It explains how a deletion was classified.

deleted-unreferenced.statement: Test-selection rule: a deleted source file has no remaining referrer, so no test needs to run for it.
deleted-unreferenced.fix: Not a defect. It explains how a deletion was classified.

dependent.statement: Test-selection rule: a test was selected because it covers a source file that refers to the changed file (one hop of dependents).
dependent.fix: Not a defect. It explains why a test ran; reach beyond one hop is the coordinator's full gate.

double-suppression.statement: A shell command drops both stderr and the exit code (`2>/dev/null || true`, `>/dev/null 2>&1 || true` or `&>/dev/null || true`), leaving no way to notice a failure.
double-suppression.fix: Fix the code so the failure is handled, or add `# shell-audit: allow -- <reason>` inline or on the line above.

event-missing-from-catalogue.statement: The vendored contract documents an event that has no entry in `constants/events.py`.
event-missing-from-catalogue.fix: Add the event (wired, or `wired=False` plus `EXPECTED_UNWIRED` per the file's tracked-gap rule).

example-config-phantom-handler.statement: `.claude/hooks-daemon.yaml.example` configures a handler that does not exist or was retired.
example-config-phantom-handler.fix: Delete the key from the example config: retired names are exempt from the unknown-handler error, so a copied block would give no error, no handler and a false belief that a protection runs.

fail-open-inventory.statement: The enforcement path has a fail-open candidate (the guarded action proceeds because the guard could not reach a verdict) that no inventory row judges, or a row is incomplete or names a candidate that is gone.
fail-open-inventory.fix: Make it fail closed, or add a judged row to `scripts/qa/fail-open-boundaries.yaml` stating what induces it, whether the input is caller-controlled and what trace it leaves; delete a row whose candidate is gone.

fetch-piped-to-shell.statement: A `curl` or `wget` pipes its output straight into an interpreter, so whatever the server sends is run.
fetch-piped-to-shell.fix: Download to a file, verify the bytes against a digest carried independently of them, then run it; or record the case in `scripts/qa/security-downgrade-inventory.yaml` with its note.

frozen-session-summary.statement: A tracked document carries a session-summary marker: a snapshot of one conversation whose counts freeze and whose next steps nothing updates.
frozen-session-summary.fix: Delete it, or fold the durable part into the document that owns the topic. Narrative belongs in the plan's JOURNAL/.

generated-doc-drift.statement: The committed `.claude/HOOKS-DAEMON.md` differs from what `generate-docs` produces now (the marker line is excluded).
generated-doc-drift.fix: Regenerate it (`bin/hooks-daemon generate-docs`) and commit it in the same change that altered the handler set; a daemon restart does not refresh it.

generated-doc-marker-missing.statement: The committed `.claude/HOOKS-DAEMON.md` carries no `> Generated on ... (vX.Y.Z)` marker, the durable record of the version the tracked assets were deployed from.
generated-doc-marker-missing.fix: Run `bin/hooks-daemon generate-docs` to restore the marker; `scripts/upgrade.sh` reads it.

git-scan-failed.statement: The history sweep could not run git, the target is not a git repository, or git reported zero commits, so no history was vouched for.
git-scan-failed.fix: Make `git` work in the target repository (path, permissions), then re-run; a sweep that scanned no commits is not a pass.

handler-claim-mismatch.statement: A document bullet's verb asserts blocking for an advisory or context handler, or advisory-only behaviour for a blocking or terminal one.
handler-claim-mismatch.fix: Correct the bullet to say what the handler does, as `.claude/HOOKS-DAEMON.md` records it.

handler-count-unverifiable.statement: A document gives a prose "N production handlers" count, which no artefact substantiates (the generated doc counts only what is enabled in this project).
handler-count-unverifiable.fix: Drop the number; say "a large library of production handlers" and point at the generated doc.

handler-ref-unknown.statement: A document names a handler that is not in the generated registry (`.claude/HOOKS-DAEMON.md`) or the handler code.
handler-ref-unknown.fix: Correct the key, delete the section if the handler does not exist, or regenerate the doc (`hooks-daemon generate-docs`) if the handler is new.

hostile-path-unguarded-command.statement: `date` or `pgrep` is looked up on PATH in a declared hostile-PATH file (the venv bootstrap and install scripts), with no `command -v` guard anywhere in the file.
hostile-path-unguarded-command.fix: Guard it with `command -v <cmd>` and a fallback (see `scripts/lib/portable_time.sh`), or add `# shell-audit: allow -- <reason>` inline or on the line above if the call cannot be reached with a hostile PATH.

ignored-plan-document.statement: A plan document is silently ignored by .gitignore, so it is missing for everyone except its author.
ignored-plan-document.fix: Narrow the .gitignore pattern (anchor a root-level name with a leading slash), then `git add` the document. Do not rename the document to dodge the pattern.

inline-suppression-without-reason.statement: An inline QA suppression (nosec, noqa including the file-wide ruff/flake8 forms, type: ignore, pyright, mypy, pylint, nosemgrep, pragma: no cover, shellcheck disable) names no reason; owner ruling B2 requires one. A bare Bandit code or test name after nosec is not a reason.
inline-suppression-without-reason.fix: Add the reason after the directive (`nosec B404 - fixed argv, no shell`), in a second `#` segment of the same comment, or in the comment block directly above that names the suppression, its code or the tool. A comment about something else does not count. Better: fix the code so the suppression can go.

install-mode-marker.statement: A file other than the two definitions (`daemon/install_layout.py`, `scripts/install/mode_guard.sh`) tests whether `src/claude_code_hooks_daemon` exists on a root the caller supplied, in order to decide the install mode. A third copy of the test drifts: three of the first four Python copies used `.exists()` where the rule is `.is_dir()`.
install-mode-marker.fix: Python: call `daemon.install_layout.is_self_install_mode` or `get_untracked_dir`; a script that runs without the package loads `install_layout.py` by file path, as `daemon/signal_standalone.py` does. Shell: source `scripts/install/mode_guard.sh` and call `is_self_install_checkout`. Building the path to SCAN the source tree, or testing a path deeper than the package directory, is not reported. There is no exemption marker.

install-mode-marker-unreadable.statement: The install-mode-marker check could not read a Python or shell file (unreadable or not UTF-8), so it cannot be shown free of an install-mode test.
install-mode-marker-unreadable.fix: Make the file readable UTF-8, or remove it if it is not source.

kill-command.statement: Python runs a `kill`, `pkill` or `killall` argv through `subprocess` (other than `kill -0`). `pkill` and `killall` pick their targets by pattern, so no pid is proven. The shell form is `shell-unproven-kill`.
kill-command.fix: Signal through `claude_code_hooks_daemon.utils.safe_signal` (`signal_verified_daemon`, `stop_verified_daemon`, `signal_own_session_child`), or signal the Popen object itself. There is no exemption marker.

log-and-continue.statement: An exception handler only logs and carries on, so the failure is indistinguishable from success.
log-and-continue.fix: Re-raise, return an error, or use `utils.deliberate_swallow.log_and_continue(..., reason=...)` if the swallow is deliberate.

log-helper-stdout.statement: A shell logging helper (`print_*`, `log_*`, `warn_*`, `err_*`) writes to stdout, which corrupts any value its caller captures.
log-helper-stdout.fix: Redirect every echo or printf in the helper with `>&2`.

magic-config-key.statement: A config key is written as a string literal when subscripting a config-like mapping instead of a constant.

magic-decision.statement: A decision value ("allow", "deny") is passed as a string literal to `decision=` instead of an enum member.

magic-event-type.statement: An event type is compared as a string literal instead of a constant.

magic-handler-display-name.statement: A handler display name is written as a string literal in a test instead of being read from the handler constant.

magic-handler-name.statement: A handler name is written as a string literal in `Handler.__init__`.

magic-priority.statement: A handler priority is written as a number instead of a constant.

magic-tag.statement: A handler tag is written as a string literal instead of a constant.

magic-timeout.statement: A timeout is written as a number, or a `settimeout()` literal guards a dispatch round trip.
magic-timeout.fix: Use the `Timeout.<NAME>` constant; a `settimeout()` literal guarding a connect-only liveness probe is correct by design and not flagged.

magic-tool-name.statement: A Claude Code tool name is written as a string literal instead of a constant.

malformed-allowlist-entry.statement: An entry in a contract allowlist (`ALLOWLIST.yaml`, `INPUT-ALLOWLIST.yaml`) lacks its `id`, its `reason` or its `link` to a plan or task.
malformed-allowlist-entry.fix: Give the entry an `id`, a `reason` and a `link` to the plan or task that tracks it, or delete it.

marker-missing-reason.statement: An `allow` marker (`shell-audit: allow`, `capture-audit: allow`) has no `-- <reason>` suffix.
marker-missing-reason.fix: Write `-- <why this is safe>` after the marker, or fix the line and remove the marker.

missing-identifier.statement: A documented `Handler` subclass calls `super().__init__()` with neither `handler_id` nor `name`, which raises ValueError.

missing-refusal-claim.statement: The docs document blocking for an event, but `REFUSAL_CAPABLE_EVENTS` omits it, so a DENY there is silently dropped.
missing-refusal-claim.fix: Add the event to `REFUSAL_CAPABLE_EVENTS`, or record why the daemon cannot express a refusal there in the contract allowlist.

module-too-long.statement: A module under `src/` is longer than 1000 lines. The check is report-only and does not gate.
module-too-long.fix: Split the module along its existing seams.

orphaned-handler-guidance.statement: The resident CLAUDE.md guidance block describes a handler that has no module in the tree.
orphaned-handler-guidance.fix: Restart the daemon so the injector regenerates the block, then commit the regenerated CLAUDE.md. Do not hand-edit the block.

plan-stats-arithmetic.statement: The plan index's reconciliation bullet carries figures (folder counts, distinct plan numbers, folderless numbers) that do not add up.
plan-stats-arithmetic.fix: Recount from disk and correct the bullet so every figure agrees with the others; do not just adjust whichever number the message names, and do not leave the verified tick above numbers that disagree.

positional-arg.statement: A documented snippet passes a positional argument to a symbol whose parameters are keyword-only.

post-upgrade-index-drift.statement: The post-upgrade task index names a task file that is gone, or omits one that exists.
post-upgrade-index-drift.fix: Add a row for each task with none and delete the row for each task that is gone.

priority-mismatch.statement: A documented handler priority differs from the priority in the code.
priority-mismatch.fix: Correct the document to the value in `constants/priority.py`.

priority-unresolvable.statement: A document gives a priority for a handler whose priority is not declared in `constants/priority.py`, so the number cannot be verified.
priority-unresolvable.fix: Add a Priority constant for the handler and use it in its `__init__` (preferred), or drop the Priority row rather than assert an unverifiable number.

public-pattern.statement: Content matches a named public sensitive-content pattern, or a configured pattern is not a valid regex and so checked nothing. The ID is `public-pattern:<name>`; the name says which pattern.
public-pattern.fix: Remove or rewrite the matched text, or fix the pattern's regex. The pattern is declared in `.claude/hooks-daemon.yaml` under `sensitive_content`.

qa-check-count-hardcoded.statement: A document hard-codes how many QA checks exist, and the number goes stale.
qa-check-count-hardcoded.fix: Remove the number and say "all checks in the QA suite" instead: no generated artefact holds the count, so it drifts silently.

raw-signal.statement: `os.kill`, `os.killpg`, `signal.pthread_kill` or `signal.pidfd_send_signal` sends a nonzero signal to a target nothing proved is the intended process.
raw-signal.fix: Route the signal through `claude_code_hooks_daemon.utils.safe_signal` (`signal_verified_daemon`, `stop_verified_daemon`, `signal_own_session_child`), or signal the Popen object itself. Signal 0 is exempt. There is no exemption marker: fix the site.

raw-stat-predicate.statement: A handler that can receive a caller-supplied path judges it with a raw `Path.exists()`, `is_file()` or `is_dir()`, which raises PermissionError when an ancestor directory is not traversable.
raw-stat-predicate.fix: Use `utils.path_predicates` (for example `path_is_file(path, unreadable_means=...)`), stating what this site means by "I could not look". For a daemon-controlled path, record `# eacces-safe-exempt: <why this path is not caller-supplied>` in place.

reference.statement: Test-selection rule: a test was selected because it is the changed file's mirrored test, or refers to it by path, by basename or by import.
reference.fix: Not a defect. It explains why a test ran.

released-changelog-section-edited.statement: CHANGELOG.md edits a section already released at the latest tag; released history is frozen.
released-changelog-section-edited.fix: Revert the edit. New notes go in `CLAUDE/UPGRADES/UNRELEASED/release-notes/`; the release process writes the CHANGELOG section.

return-none-on-error.statement: A handler returns None on error instead of raising, so the caller cannot tell failure from absence.
return-none-on-error.fix: Raise a specific exception, or return a result type that carries the error.

return-none-via-local.statement: A handler binds None or an empty default to a local that is returned after the try: return-none-on-error in a different spelling.
return-none-via-local.fix: Re-raise, log at warning or above, or record the problem on a list the function returns or reports; or return a result type that carries the error.

root-test-script.statement: A `test_*.sh` script sits at the repository root, where nothing owns or runs it.
root-test-script.fix: Move it into `tests/` (or beside the code it exercises) if it still earns its keep, otherwise delete it.

secret-word-list.statement: Content matches an entry of the gitignored secret word list. Only the entry index is reported, never the term.
secret-word-list.fix: Remove the matched text. Ask the owner what the entry covers; do not open the secret word list.

security-downgrade-flag.statement: A script sets a flag whose only effect is to turn a protection off (`--no-verify`, `verify=False`, `PYTHONHTTPSVERIFY=0`, `-k` or `--insecure` on a fetching line, ...).
security-downgrade-flag.fix: Remove the flag, or record the case in `scripts/qa/security-downgrade-inventory.yaml` with its reason.

self.statement: Test-selection rule: a changed test file selects itself.
self.fix: Not a defect. It explains why a test ran.

shell-discard-both-streams.statement: A shell command redirects stdout to /dev/null and then stderr to the same place (`>/dev/null 2>&1`), so its failures leave no trace.
shell-discard-both-streams.fix: Redirect only what you intend; log errors to a file or stderr.

shell-empty-err-trap.statement: A shell file installs an empty ERR trap (`trap '' ERR`), which silences every command failure the trap would have reported.
shell-empty-err-trap.fix: Remove the trap or handle errors explicitly.

shell-or-colon.statement: A shell command ends in `|| :`, which turns its failure into success.
shell-or-colon.fix: Handle failure explicitly with if/else or exit 1.

shell-or-true.statement: A shell command ends in `|| true`, which turns its failure into success.
shell-or-true.fix: Handle failure explicitly with if/else or exit 1.

shell-redirect-all-to-null.statement: A shell command sends both stdout and stderr to /dev/null with `&>/dev/null`, so its failures leave no trace.
shell-redirect-all-to-null.fix: Redirect only what you intend; log errors to a file or stderr.

shell-set-plus-e.statement: A shell file turns errexit off with `set +e`, so a failing command no longer stops the script.
shell-set-plus-e.fix: Remove `set +e`; handle individual command failures with if/else.

shell-unproven-kill.statement: A shell `kill`, `pkill` or `killall` in command position sends a nonzero signal to a target nothing proved. `pkill` and `killall` pick targets by pattern and are always reported; a `kill` target is proven only when it is `$$`, `$!`, a `%job`, a variable always bound to `$!`, or a variable an identity check ran on earlier in the same function.
shell-unproven-kill.fix: Run an identity check on the pid earlier in the same function (`_is_project_daemon_pid`, a start-time or parent check), or signal `$$` or `$!`. A group target (`-PGID`) needs an identity check. There is no exemption marker.

silent-continue.statement: An exception handler whose whole body is `continue` skips the error with no trace.
silent-continue.fix: Record the skipped item where the caller reads it (append it to a list the function returns or reports, or tell the user on the console), call `utils.deliberate_swallow.log_and_continue(..., reason=...)` if the skip is deliberate, or let the error propagate. A bare log call plus `continue` is `log-and-continue`.

silent-fallback.statement: An exception handler whose whole body is one assignment replaces the error with a fallback value, with no logging or re-raise, so failure looks like success.
silent-fallback.fix: Re-raise, surface the failure (log at warning or above, or `utils.deliberate_swallow.log_and_continue(..., reason=...)`) alongside the fallback, or let the error propagate. A logged None or empty default is `log-and-continue`.

silent-pass.statement: An exception handler whose whole body is `pass` swallows the error completely. Narrowing the exception type does not change the finding.
silent-pass.fix: Handle the error or let it propagate. If the swallow is deliberate, call `utils.deliberate_swallow.log_and_continue(..., reason=...)` with a specific reason.

slash-command-in-shell-fence.statement: A Claude Code slash command is shown inside a shell-tagged code fence.

slash-command-syntax.statement: An agent-facing string uses `/hooks-daemon` slash-command syntax, which Claude interprets as a bash command.
slash-command-syntax.fix: Point the agent at the skill instead: `Skill tool: skill=hooks-daemon, args=<subcommand>`.

src-test-stub.statement: A test file sits under `src/`, where pytest never collects it, so it runs nowhere.
src-test-stub.fix: Delete it and write the real test under `tests/`. Never commit a bypass of the TDD gate.

stale-allowlist-entry.statement: An allowlist entry excuses a finding that no longer exists.
stale-allowlist-entry.fix: Delete the entry; the allowlist must only hold live exceptions.

stale-exclusion.statement: An entry of `error_hiding_exclusions.json` matches no finding, so it drifted off its target or the code was fixed.
stale-exclusion.fix: Realign the entry to its target, or delete it.

stale-grandfather.statement: A grandfathered ref in the history sweep's configuration no longer exists.

suppressed-fetch.statement: A `curl`, `wget` or `git clone` discards its failure to /dev/null, so a fetch that went wrong cannot be seen.
suppressed-fetch.fix: Let the fetch report failure and check its exit status.

tracked-build-artifact.statement: A build artefact is tracked in the repository.
tracked-build-artifact.fix: Untrack it (`git rm --cached`) and ignore the path.

unauditable-file.statement: A file could not be opened or decoded, so it was never audited for error hiding.
unauditable-file.fix: Make the file readable UTF-8, or remove it; an unaudited file is not a pass.

unbounded-skip-list-membership.statement: A skip or exclude list entry is tested against a path with bare `in`, which is substring containment, so the guard stands down for any path that merely ends in the entry.
unbounded-skip-list-membership.fix: Use `utils.path_segments.matches_path_segment(file_path, patterns, project_root=resolve_project_root())`, which matches whole path segments relative to the project.

undocumented-blocking-handler.statement: A PreToolUse blocking handler listed in the generated `.claude/HOOKS-DAEMON.md` has no section in the canonical `docs/guides/HANDLER_REFERENCE.md`.
undocumented-blocking-handler.fix: Add a `#### <key>` section for the handler to `docs/guides/HANDLER_REFERENCE.md`.

undocumented-claim.statement: `REFUSAL_CAPABLE_EVENTS` claims DENY or ASK on an event for which the docs document no such mechanism.
undocumented-claim.fix: Remove the claim, or refresh the contract if Claude Code now documents it.

undocumented-emitted-token.statement: Serialising a DENY on an event emits a top-level `decision` token the docs never define.
undocumented-emitted-token.fix: Emit a documented decision value, or refresh the contract.

undocumented-enum-value.statement: A schema enum allows a value the docs do not define for that event.
undocumented-enum-value.fix: Remove the value, or refresh the contract.

undocumented-schema-field.statement: A schema accepts a field (top-level, `hookSpecificOutput.*` or nested) the docs do not define for that event.
undocumented-schema-field.fix: Remove the field, or refresh the contract.

unexpressed-capability.statement: The docs define a field the daemon's schema for that event cannot express.
unexpressed-capability.fix: Add the field to the schema, or record why the daemon omits it in the contract allowlist.

unexpressed-enum-value.statement: The docs define an enum value of a `hookSpecificOutput` field that the daemon's schema cannot express.
unexpressed-enum-value.fix: Add the value, or record why the daemon omits it in the contract allowlist.

unexpressed-universal-fields.statement: An event's schema cannot express the documented universal output fields (`continue`, `stopReason`, `suppressOutput`, `systemMessage`, `terminalSequence`).
unexpressed-universal-fields.fix: Add the missing universal fields to the event's output schema.

unknown-import.statement: A documented snippet imports a name the package does not export.
unknown-import.fix: Correct the import to a real name, or remove the snippet.

unknown-input-field.statement: The daemon reads a hook-input field the vendored per-event examples do not contain.
unknown-input-field.fix: Stop reading the field; or, if it arrives only under some condition, declare it with that condition in the event's `conditional_input_fields`; or refresh the vendored examples if Claude Code now sends it.

unknown-keyword.statement: A documented snippet passes a keyword the callee does not accept (a Pydantic model may silently discard it).
unknown-keyword.fix: Use a keyword the callee has.

unparseable-shell.statement: A quote, `$(...)`, backtick or heredoc opened in a shell file never closes, so the lines after it cannot be audited as logical commands.
unparseable-shell.fix: Fix the unterminated quote, backtick, `$(...)` or heredoc.

unproven-process-handle.statement: `.terminate()`, `.kill()` or `.send_signal()` is called on a `psutil.Process` built from a raw pid or taken from `psutil.process_iter()`, or `.send_signal()` on a receiver not proven to be a `subprocess.Popen` this scope spawned.
unproven-process-handle.fix: Signal through `claude_code_hooks_daemon.utils.safe_signal`, or through a handle it returned (`verified_daemon_process`), or signal the Popen itself. An inline check of the handle's command line or start time is not proof. There is no exemption marker.

unreachable-handle-branch.statement: A handler's `handle()` does work under `if not self.matches(...)`, which the chain never executes.
unreachable-handle-branch.fix: Make `matches()` return True for every input `handle()` must see and let `handle()` choose the decision; keep the `if not self.matches(...)` branch, if at all, as a bare `return` of an ALLOW.

unreadable-file.statement: A file could not be read, decoded or tokenised, so it was never checked.
unreadable-file.fix: Make the file readable UTF-8, or fix the parse error the finding names; an unread file is not a pass.

unreleased-manifest-date.statement: A released config-changes manifest still carries the UNRELEASED placeholder, or any other non-ISO `date:`, instead of its release date.
unreleased-manifest-date.fix: Set `date:` to the date the version was tagged (`git log -1 --format=%cs vX.Y.Z`) when the manifest moves out of UNRELEASED.

unset-shell-variable-in-guidance.statement: Agent-facing guidance names a shell variable (such as `$PYTHON`) that is never set in an agent's shell.
unset-shell-variable-in-guidance.fix: Use `utils.cli_command.daemon_cli_command(...)` so the emitted command is an absolute path to the deployed `bin/hooks-daemon` wrapper; in static markdown, write the wrapper path directly.

unvalidated-url-expansion.statement: A URL is built from an environment expansion that nothing scheme-checks, in a file that fetches.
unvalidated-url-expansion.fix: Validate the scheme (https only) before fetching.

wrong-github-owner.statement: A GitHub URL names this project under an owner that is not the canonical repository.
